chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article I — Overnight Guests
chunks.text:
Members may host overnight guests in their own private rooms. Any single
guest may stay no more than two consecutive nights within any seven-day
period, so that no guest gradually becomes an unofficial resident of the
house. Whenever a guest is in the shared common areas, the hosting member
must accompany them. Each member is fully responsible for the conduct of
their guests for the entire duration of the visit.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article II — Quiet Hours
chunks.text:
Quiet hours are observed every night, running from 11:00 PM until 7:00 AM
the following morning. During quiet hours, conversation in the common areas
must be kept low, and any music, television, or video games must be played
through headphones. A member who anticipates unavoidable late-night noise
is required to give the rest of the house advance notice so that everyone
can reliably sleep.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article III — Kitchen Cleanup
chunks.text:
The kitchen must be cleaned by whoever used it, immediately after that
person finishes cooking or eating. Cleaning means washing every dish you
used, wiping down the counters and the stovetop, and taking out the trash
when the bin is full. Leaving dirty dishes in the sink overnight is never
permitted, no matter how late the hour or how tired the cook.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article IV — Common Spaces
chunks.text:
The living room, the dining room, and the back porch are common areas that
belong equally to every member of the house. No member may reserve a common
area for their own exclusive use, even temporarily, and no member may treat
a common area as a personal extension of their bedroom. These shared spaces
must remain open and available to all members at all times.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article V — Shared Chores
chunks.text:
All members share the household chores equally, following the rotating
weekly schedule posted in the kitchen. Every member is assigned the same
number of chore slots each month, and no member is exempt from the rotation
for any reason whatsoever. A member who cannot complete an assigned chore is
required to arrange a direct swap with another member ahead of time.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article VI — Pets
chunks.text:
No member may keep a pet of any kind in the house, with the single exception
of fish kept in a tank no larger than twenty gallons. This rule exists to
protect members who have allergies and to avoid noise, odor, and damage to
the shared furnishings. A member who wishes to pet-sit an animal for someone
outside the house must obtain unanimous consent from all members first.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article VII — Smoking
chunks.text:
Smoking of any kind is forbidden everywhere inside the house, including
inside a member's own private bedroom. The prohibition covers cigarettes,
cigars, pipes, and vaporizers alike. It exists to keep the shared air clean
and to reduce the risk of fire. Each member is responsible for ensuring that
their visitors also refrain from smoking indoors during any visit.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article VIII — Rent and Dues
chunks.text:
Each member must pay their share of the rent on or before the first day of
every month by transferring it to the house account. The monthly house dues
that cover shared cleaning supplies and paper goods are due on that same day.
A member who anticipates any difficulty paying on time is required to notify
the house treasurer before the first of the month.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article IX — Personal Belongings
chunks.text:
Members must keep their personal belongings in their own bedrooms or in
their assigned storage space. A personal item left in a common area for more
than one full day may be moved by any other member to the owner's bedroom
door. Perishable personal food left out in a common area may be thrown away
after a day. This keeps the shared spaces usable for everyone.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article X — House Decisions
chunks.text:
The house meets on the first Sunday of every month to make decisions
together. A decision passes by a simple majority of the members present, and
a recorded decision amends or extends this Charter from the date it is made.
Any member may place an item on the meeting agenda by posting it on the
kitchen board at least two days before the meeting.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-01-12 — Guest Logbook
chunks.text:
To keep track of who is in the house at any time, the members resolved that
every overnight guest must be signed into the guest logbook kept by the
front door, recording the guest's name and the dates of their stay. The
hosting member is responsible for making the entry before the guest's first
night. This record is meant to help with safety and accountability.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-02-10 — Weeknight Quiet Hours
chunks.text:
After repeated complaints about noise on work nights, the house met and
resolved to move the start of quiet hours earlier during the week. Effective
immediately, quiet hours now begin at 10:00 PM on Sunday through Thursday
nights, a full hour earlier than the Charter originally set. The 7:00 AM end
time and the Friday and Saturday start times are left unchanged.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-02-24 — Backyard Quiet
chunks.text:
Following complaints about late gatherings outdoors, the house resolved that
the quiet-hours rule also applies to the backyard and the back porch, not
only to the indoor common areas. During quiet hours, members and any guests
must keep outdoor conversation low and must not run outdoor speakers. This
decision extends the existing quiet hours rather than changing their times.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-03-14 — Guest Policy Revisited
chunks.text:
Following a long discussion about privacy, crowding, and the shared cost of
utilities, the house resolved to stop allowing overnight guests altogether.
Effective this month, overnight guests are no longer permitted in the house
at any time, for any number of nights, in any bedroom. Members may still
host visitors during the daytime, but every visitor must leave by 10:00 PM.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-03-28 — Guest Parking
chunks.text:
To settle ongoing confusion about where visitors should leave their cars,
the house resolved to set aside the two marked spaces at the far end of the
driveway specifically for visitor and guest parking. Guests are welcome to
leave a vehicle parked in those two spaces overnight without needing any
permit. This decision is strictly about parking and changes nothing about
whether or how long guests may stay in the house.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-04-02 — Cooking and Cleanup
chunks.text:
Recognizing that whichever member cooks dinner for the whole house already
contributes a great deal of effort, the house resolved that whoever cooks
the shared house dinner is excused from cleaning the kitchen on that night.
On those evenings, the work of washing the dishes, wiping the counters, and
taking out the trash falls instead to the members who sat down and ate.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-04-18 — Fridge Labeling
chunks.text:
To cut down on food going to waste and on disputes over groceries, the house
resolved that members must label their personal food in the shared
refrigerator with their name and the date it was placed there. Any unlabeled
food in the fridge may be treated as communal and eaten by anyone in the
house. This decision adds to the kitchen rules rather than replacing them.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-05-06 — Dining Room Reservations
chunks.text:
To make room for the occasional birthday or study group, the house resolved
that a member may reserve the dining room for their own private event up to
twice a month by signing the shared calendar at least three days ahead. For
the booked hours of a reserved event, the dining room is closed to the other
members so that the host can use the space.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-05-20 — Travel Chore Exemption
chunks.text:
Recognizing that several members travel frequently for work, the house
resolved that any member who is away from the house for more than two
consecutive weeks is fully exempt from the chore rotation for the entire
period they are gone. The remaining members will quietly cover the absent
member's chore slots, and the absent member owes no make-up chores on return.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-06-03 — House Cat
chunks.text:
After a heartfelt request and a long debate, the house resolved by majority
vote to allow one house cat, to be adopted and cared for collectively by the
members. The cat is permitted only if every current member gives written
approval beforehand, and it must be kept out of the bedroom of any member who
objects on the grounds of allergies.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-06-10 — Porch Smoking
chunks.text:
In response to requests from members who smoke, the house resolved that
smoking is now permitted outdoors on the back porch only, provided that the
smoker uses the sand bucket and sits at least ten feet away from any open
window. Smoking of every kind remains completely forbidden everywhere inside
the house, exactly as before.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-06-15 — Late Rent Fee
chunks.text:
To encourage everyone to pay on time, the house resolved that a member whose
rent share has not arrived in the house account by the fifth day of the
month owes an additional late fee of twenty-five dollars on top of the rent.
The treasurer will send a reminder to all members two days before the
monthly deadline.

chunks.heading: Maple House Charter, Article XI — Quiet Study Hours
chunks.text:
The dining room is set aside as a silent study space every weeknight from
7:00 PM until 9:00 PM. During those hours the dining room is reserved for
quiet individual work and may not be used for meals, conversation, or
gatherings. Members who need to eat during that window should use the
kitchen or their own rooms so that the study hours stay undisturbed for
those who are working.

chunks.heading: Decision — 2026-06-22 — Thursday Movie Nights
chunks.text:
To give the house a shared social evening, the members resolved to hold a
movie night in the living room on Thursday evenings. On those nights the
film and the conversation around it may run in the living room until
midnight, and any member who wishes to take part is welcome to stay up that
late. Members who would rather have quiet on a Thursday should plan around
the movie night.

tensions.reason: A member is assigned a mandatory household chore (such as deep cleaning the bathroom) that must be completed during quiet hours or while their guest is in a common area; fulfilling the chore requires leaving the shared space to work on it, which directly violates the requirement that the hosting member accompany any single guest whenever they are in those areas.

A member anticipates unavoidable late-night noise from an event occurring after 11:00 PM and gives advance notice as required, but this action inherently conflicts with the strict observance of quiet hours, creating a situation where complying with one rule necessitates violating the other.

A guest is in the shared common areas during quiet hours (11:00 PM to 7:00 AM), requiring the hosting member to accompany them; however, if the host must leave for work or sleep before 7:00 AM, they cannot fulfill the accompaniment requirement while also observing their own need for rest or external obligations that prevent staying awake until morning.

The rule limiting a single guest to two consecutive nights within any seven-day period conflicts with full responsibility for conduct over the entire duration of the visit when a guest stays exactly two nights but causes significant damage on the second night; the host is liable for the 'entire duration' including the restricted final night where supervision might be less intensive due to the impending departure, yet liability remains absolute regardless of the time limit's intent to reduce long-term exposure.
On a Tuesday night at 10:30 PM, the commitment that quiet hours begin at 11:00 PM conflicts with the specific rule for Sunday through Thursday nights stating they begin at 10:00 PM.

When a member cooks the shared house dinner and uses dishes in doing so, the requirement to clean the kitchen immediately after finishing cooking contradicts the exemption from cleaning on that same night.

The commitment that quiet hours are observed every night from 11:00 PM until 7:00 AM conflicts with the allowance for movie nights to run until midnight in the living room. A member cannot simultaneously honor the strict silence required during quiet hours and participate in a loud social gathering scheduled to end at midnight.

The rule requiring music or television to be played through headphones during quiet hours (starting at 11:00 PM) is incompatible with hosting a group movie night in the common area that runs until midnight. The nature of a shared movie viewing requires audible sound from speakers, which violates the headphone mandate active during the final hour of the event.

A member seeks to pet-sit a dog for one week and requests unanimous consent from all members as required by the specific rule. However, if only half of the house is present at the monthly meeting (or via written ballot), they can pass an amendment under the simple majority rule that lowers the threshold for future external pet-sitting approvals or grants blanket permission, thereby overriding the requirement for unanimity in subsequent cases.

A member who is assigned to cook the shared house dinner (and thus excused from cleaning) cannot complete their other assigned chore and must arrange a direct swap ahead of time; however, if they are also responsible for cooking that night, the specific exemption for the cook conflicts with the general requirement to manage all non-completed chores via swaps before the fact.

An overnight guest arrives at the front door requiring immediate sign-in in the logbook, but this same person has come specifically to pet-sit an animal inside the house; obtaining unanimous consent from *all* members (including those asleep or away) is impossible in real-time upon arrival, forcing a choice between admitting them without full consent or refusing entry despite their signed status as a guest.

The house collectively adopts a cat (Commitment 14), but the general rule forbids keeping any pet other than fish in tanks no larger than twenty gallons (Commitment 2). Since a cat is not a fish and cannot be kept in such a tank, these two commitments directly contradict each other regarding what animals are permitted to live in the house.

A daytime visitor who arrives before 10:00 PM and intends to stay overnight must leave by the deadline set for 'daytime visitors,' yet they are explicitly permitted to use the reserved parking spaces 'overnight without a permit.' The situation forces a choice between enforcing the departure time or allowing the guest to remain in their vehicle.

On a Thursday night, quiet hours begin at 10:00 PM while movie nights are permitted to run until midnight. A member cannot simultaneously honor the requirement that outdoor conversation be kept low and speakers not used during quiet hours if they wish to participate in or host a loud movie screening past 10:00 PM.

The commitments state that quiet hours apply to the backyard and back porch (Commitment 4) but then specify that members must keep *outdoor* conversation low and not use speakers (Commitment 5). If a member is on the back porch at 11:00 PM, Commitment 3 requires silence/quiet, yet Commitment 5 explicitly regulates 'outdoor' behavior; however, the tension arises because Commitment 22 allows movie nights in the living room until midnight. While this seems like an indoor/outdoor distinction, let's look closer. Actually, Commitments 3, 4, and 5 are consistent with each other regarding quiet hours. Let's re-evaluate.

Let's look at **Commitment 6** vs **Commitment 7**. 
Commitment 6 says daytime visitors must leave by 10:00 PM. 
Commitment 7 says visitor parking may be used overnight without a permit. 
This is not necessarily a direct conflict if 'visitor' implies someone staying over? No, usually 'daytime visitor' means non-guest. But if they stay overnight, they become guests (Commitment 2). If they don't sign in, they violate Commitment 2. This isn't a clear tension between the rules themselves unless we assume a specific scenario.

Let's look at **Commitment 1** vs **Commitment 3/4/5**. 
No obvious conflict.

Let's look at **Commitment 8** vs **Commitment 9/10**? No.

Let's look at **Commitment 16** vs **Commitment 17**. 
Cat must be kept out of bedroom of allergic member. Smoking on back porch is allowed if away from windows. If the allergic member sleeps in a room with an open window facing the back porch, and the smoker uses the sand bucket but smoke drifts? The rule says 'sit at least ten feet away'. It doesn't guarantee no smell/smoke entry. But this is weak.

Let's re-examine **Commitment 3 (Quiet Hours)** vs **Commitment 22 (Movie Nights)**. 
Commitment 3: Quiet hours begin at 10:00 PM Sunday-Thursday.
Commitment 4: Applies to backyard/porch AND indoor common areas.
Commitment 5: During quiet hours... keep outdoor conversation low...
Wait, Commitment 5 only mentions *outdoor* conversation and speakers. Does it cover indoor noise? Usually 'quiet hours' implies general noise reduction. However, Commitment 20 defines a specific silent study space in the dining room on weeknights 7-9 PM. It does not define what happens in other rooms during quiet hours (10 PM+).
If Movie Night is in the Living Room (a common area) until Midnight, and Quiet Hours apply to Indoor Common Areas from 10 PM onwards, there is a direct conflict for Thursday nights between 10:00 PM and midnight.
The member hosting/participating must choose between honoring the movie night duration or adhering to the quiet hour restrictions for indoor common areas.

A daytime visitor who decides to stay overnight becomes an 'overnight guest' requiring sign-in before their first night. However, Commitment 6 mandates that all daytime visitors leave by 10:00 PM. A situation arises where a visitor arrives during the day but wishes to sleep over; they cannot both remain in the house past 10:00 PM (violating Commitment 6) and fulfill the requirement of being signed into the logbook as an overnight guest for that same night if they are forced out.

On Thursday evenings between 7:00 PM and 9:00 PM, the dining room is designated as a silent study space where conversation is prohibited, while movie nights are held in the living room during this same time window. If members gather to watch the movie together or discuss it, they must either violate the silence rule by conversing in the dining area (if they move there) or risk disturbing the quiet study environment from adjacent spaces if the noise carries over, creating a conflict between enforcing strict silence for studying and facilitating social movie viewing.
